paragraphs: All six directions are premised on "assessment and communication", but the objects, authorization, and responsibility boundaries differ; the same assessment or rehabilitation experience cannot be directly converted into another direction's practice licensure or prescription authority, and this page only compares responsibility differences under public definitions.

The comparison basis is the official occupation description and related occupations list for O*NET 29-1181.00, and the adjacent occupation relationships labeled in the routing materials; an adjacent relationship only indicates that duties are close and does not mean that qualifications, licensure, or authorization are interchangeable.

The table below compares audiologists with five adjacent directions on the same set of dimensions: occupation direction, core work and outputs, key differences, and which choice better suits each preference.

Focuses on hearing aid selection, fitting, and after-sales service and usually does not carry diagnostic and prescription responsibility; audiologists carry audiological assessment, differential interpretation, and intervention plan development.

If you would rather do hearing aid selection and customer service, compare hearing aid specialists first; if you would rather do audiological assessment and plan development, then audiologists suit you.
Carrying out hearing aid selection, fitting and programming, outcome verification, and after-sales maintenance, with outputs mainly fitting and after-sales records.
Audiologists and hearing aid specialists

Centered on assessment and treatment of speech and language disorders, with attention to articulation, language comprehension, and expression; audiologists center on assessment and intervention for hearing and balance function.
If you would rather deal with speech and language disorders, compare speech-language pathologists first; if you would rather deal with hearing and balance disorders, then audiologists suit you.
Assessing speech and language ability and developing and implementing treatment plans, with outputs mainly treatment records and progress evaluations.
Audiologists and speech-language pathologists
Focuses on visual function examination and refractive correction, with the visual system as its object; audiologists focus on the auditory and vestibular systems.
If you would rather do visual function examination and refractive correction, compare optometrists first; if you would rather do hearing and balance assessment, then audiologists suit you.
Examining vision and refractive status and fitting glasses or contact lenses, with outputs mainly optometric prescriptions and examination records.
Audiologists and optometrists
Focuses on functional training for daily living activities and environmental modification, serving a broader population; audiologists' intervention is more concentrated on hearing and communication.

If you would rather do functional training and improving independent living ability, compare occupational therapists first; if you would rather focus on hearing and communication, then audiologists suit you.
Assessing occupational performance and designing and implementing functional training, with outputs mainly training plans and functional assessments.
Audiologists and occupational therapists
Focuses on assessment and training of motor function and pain; audiologists focus on auditory and vestibular function.
If you would rather do motor function rehabilitation, compare physical therapists first; if you would rather do hearing and balance rehabilitation, then audiologists suit you.
Assessing motor function and implementing therapeutic exercise and manual therapy, with outputs mainly treatment records and functional assessments.
Audiologists and physical therapists
Focuses on the diagnosis and treatment of nervous system diseases, which may involve surgery and medication; audiologists focus on audiological assessment and rehabilitation intervention.
If you would rather diagnose and treat nervous system diseases, compare neurologists first; if you would rather do audiological assessment and rehabilitation, then audiologists suit you.
Diagnosing and treating nervous system diseases and interpreting imaging and neuroelectrophysiology, with outputs mainly diagnoses and treatment plans.
Audiologists and neurologists

Conclusion: the basis for choosing a direction is the object, authorization, and responsibility boundaries, not whether assessment and communication are both done; after settling on a direction, verify item by item the degree, clinical training, practice licensure, and institutional authorization requirements of the target direction.

entries: The Investigative type corresponds to history analysis, interpretation and differential diagnosis of test results, and verification of device parameters and outcomes, which is the professional foundation of this occupation.

The Social type corresponds to communication and guidance with patients, families, teachers, and employers; being willing to switch back and forth between technical interpretation and communicative care is an interest signal closer to this occupation.
